article_title: I was told I had depression for 14 years until I got sectioned - it was bipolar

tasks.prompt: What is the article mainly about?
options: Why antidepressants cure every form of bipolar disorder
How universities train psychiatrists to diagnose weather-related beliefs
Why people with bipolar disorder should avoid working full-time
How bipolar disorder can be mistaken for depression for years, and why better screening matters
tasks.correct_answer: How bipolar disorder can be mistaken for depression for years, and why better screening matters
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה מתארת אבחונים מאוחרים של קימברלי וג'קי ומציגה את קריאת המומחים לשיפור הסינון למאניה ולהיפומאניה.

tasks.prompt: What event led doctors to diagnose Kimberley Atkinson with bipolar disorder?
options: She began working for the NHS.
She was admitted to a psychiatric ward after increasingly erratic and delusional behaviour.
She asked her GP for a routine family-history test.
She stopped experiencing depression while studying.
tasks.correct_answer: She was admitted to a psychiatric ward after increasingly erratic and delusional behaviour.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: לאחר התנהגות לא יציבה ומחשבות שווא, קימברלי אושפזה בניגוד לרצונה; שם הרופאים זיהו שמדובר בהפרעה דו־קוטבית.

tasks.prompt: What does “hypomania” mean as used in the article?
options: A period of unusually high energy or mood that is less severe than full mania
A form of depression caused only by medication
A controlled seizure used in hospital treatment
A complete and permanent break from reality
tasks.correct_answer: A period of unusually high energy or mood that is less severe than full mania
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה מגדירה hypomania כתקופה של אנרגיה, פעילות או מצב רוח גבוהים מהרגיל, אך פחות חמורה ממאניה מלאה.

tasks.prompt: What screening does Prof Danny Smith say health professionals should perform?
options: Ask only how long a patient has felt sad.
Check whether patients have used social media.
Ask about mania symptoms and a family history of bipolar disorder.
Refer every depressed patient directly for electroconvulsive therapy.
tasks.correct_answer: Ask about mania symptoms and a family history of bipolar disorder.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: פרופ' סמית קורא לשאול על תסמיני מאניה ועל היסטוריה משפחתית של ההפרעה כדי לזהות אפשרות של דו־קוטביות.

tasks.prompt: Why is bipolar II described as particularly difficult to diagnose?
options: It never includes depressive periods.
Its elevated periods are less severe, while depression may be more frequent and more noticeable.
It can be identified only through brain scans.
People with it always refuse psychiatric assessment.
tasks.correct_answer: Its elevated periods are less severe, while depression may be more frequent and more noticeable.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בדו־קוטביות מסוג II תקופות ההיפומאניה מתונות יותר, בעוד שהדיכאון עשוי לבלוט, ולכן האבחנה עלולה להתמקד בדיכאון בלבד.

tasks.prompt: In this article, what does “underdiagnosed” mean?
options: Diagnosed immediately in every case
Treated only with talking therapy
Caused by a lack of sleep
Identified in fewer people than probably have the condition
tasks.correct_answer: Identified in fewer people than probably have the condition
tasks.explanation_hebrew: underdiagnosed פירושו שההפרעה מאובחנת אצל פחות אנשים ממספר האנשים שסביר כי חיים איתה בפועל.

tasks.prompt: How did Jacqui Armstrong's experience reveal signs of bipolar disorder beyond depression?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין את תקופות ההיפומאניה, מאפייניהן, ההידרדרות שאחריהן והאבחון לאחר שנשאלה על תסמינים אלה.
expected_points: Alongside depression, Jacqui experienced episodes of hypomania.
She described unusual confidence, many ideas, sociability and attempts to fill her diary.
She said the high energy could lead into a breakdown.
A psychiatrist finally asked about hypomania, leading to assessment and a bipolar II diagnosis.

tasks.prompt: Summarise Kimberley's path from an initial depression diagnosis to her current situation.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לתאר את 14 שנות האבחנה בדיכאון, הופעת תסמיני המאניה והאשפוז, האבחנה החדשה והיציבות לאחר טיפול מתאים.
expected_points: Kimberley was treated for depression for 14 years, but antidepressants did not explain her changing moods.
Her thinking became erratic and delusional, culminating in an involuntary psychiatric admission.
Doctors diagnosed bipolar I and she later accepted that the diagnosis explained years of symptoms.
With the right medication she is stable, works full-time for the NHS and has had no manic episode for four years.

tasks.prompt: Why might routine questions about high-energy periods shorten delays in bipolar diagnosis?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר שמטופלים פונים בדרך כלל בזמן דיכאון ולא רואים באנרגיה גבוהה בעיה, ולכן שאלות יזומות יכולות לחשוף מאניה או היפומאניה ולהוביל להפניה.
expected_points: Patients often seek help for depression rather than for feeling energetic or creative.
They may not recognise reduced sleep, racing thoughts or unusual confidence as symptoms.
Direct questions can reveal past mania or hypomania that would otherwise be missed.
Identifying those signs can prompt psychiatric referral and a more accurate diagnosis.

tasks.prompt: Write a balanced public-health message based on the article about seeking the right diagnosis for mood changes.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לעודד פנייה לאיש מקצוע, אזכור מלא של תקופות נמוכות וגבוהות והיסטוריה משפחתית, בלי אבחון עצמי; יש להדגיש שהמצב ניתן לניהול בטיפול מתאים.
expected_points: Encourage people with significant mood changes to speak to a qualified health professional.
Suggest describing both depressive periods and unusually energetic, sleepless or irritable periods.
Mention that family history may be relevant to assessment.
Avoid self-diagnosis and note that bipolar disorder can be highly manageable with proper diagnosis and treatment.
